@openllmsh/dsh - route DeepSeek Harness through OpenLLM.

A DeepSeek Harness (`dsh`)
bundle that points the harness at the OpenLLM gateway and
hands it OpenLL

M's MCP tools. It is a **pure-config Cordis patch layer**,
installed from the dsh side, with no runt
ime code. It does two things:

- **LLM router** - adds an `openllm` provider to dsh's in-box `llm-pi-ai`
adapter (`openai-completio

ns`) pointed at the daemon's **local-first gateway**
(`http://127.0.0.1:8787/v1`) and makes it the d

efault model. No adapter code,
and **no API key in dsh**: the daemon authenticates with the saved lo

map to OpenLLM `reasoning_effort`
(`none|minimal|low|medium|high|xhigh|max`).
- **MCP** - registers

the OpenLLM MCP stdio server. The command resolves to
`$HOME/.openllm/bin/openllm` (installer binar

y path) with args `['mcp']`, so
Desktop/GUI launches that do not inherit a shell `PATH` still find i

path) with args `['mcp']`, so
Desktop/GUI launches that do not inherit a shell `PATH` still find it.

dsh holds **no key and no origin** - it talks to `127.0.0.1:8787` with a
placeholder bearer that the

daemon runs as the saved login. Installing OpenLLM
and signing in are prerequisites (below). Runs o

n the host DeepSeek Harness;
the services it patches (`@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm-pi-ai`, `@deepseek-ai/ds

h-mcp-client`)
ship in `@deepseek-ai/dsh-base`.

OpenLLM routes your API keys, local vendors and local models through one
format-agnostic endpoint. S
ee the OpenLLM documentation.

## Install the bundle

Install into the profile whose surface you actually run. dsh profiles are
separate bundle stacks, so

a bundle added to one profile is invisible to the
others - the **browser UI lives only in the `web`

profile** (`web` mounts
`dsh-base` + `dsh-web-app`; `headless` mounts `dsh-base` + `dsh-headless`).

The bare `default` profile is `dsh-base` only - no web surface - so adding the
bundle there never r

Then **restart the profile**. Prefer the npm package. The GitHub spec remains an

lugin --profile web add github:openllmsh/dsh`, pin with

step (and no pnpm `allowBuilds` prompt).
## Images and reasoning

- **Images** - the `openllm` route declares `defaultInput: [text, image]`, so
attached images are ac

cepted when the resolved model supports vision.
- **Reasoning** - dsh thinking levels map to OpenLLM

`reasoning_effort` values
(`off` → `none`, then `minimal` through `max`). The route default is `med

soning_effort` values
(`off` → `none`, then `minimal` through `max`). The route default is `medium`.
## MCP binary path and startup race

The MCP entry uses `$HOME/.openllm/bin/openllm` (via Cordis `!!js`), not a bare
`openllm` on `PATH`,

so GUI hosts find the installer binary. If `HOME` is unset,
it falls back to `openllm` on `PATH`.

The first MCP tool call can fail while the OpenLLM MCP server or daemon is still
starting. `failOnSt

artupError` stays false and reconnect uses a short initial
delay; wait a moment and retry the call -
it reconnects automatically.
## Self-hosted / custom port

The router base (`http://127.0.0.1:8787/v1`) is fixed in `cordis.patch.yml`. To
route through a self

-hosted OpenLLM, point the **daemon** at your origin when you
install it - dsh still just talks to `

127.0.0.1:8787`. A custom daemon port
(`OPENLLM_DAEMON_PORT`) means editing the `baseURL` in `cordis
.patch.yml` to match.

s** - a stale `lib/` is what git installs.
